recent_posts.title: The Race Against the Clock: Optimizing Supply Chain Capacity for Faster Deliveries — Part 1 (Capacity Management Series)
recent_posts.summary: Flipkart's engineering team explains how their Promise Engine calculates delivery dates and why gaps exist between theoretical and actual delivery speeds. The core problem is 'spillage' — orders missing warehouse processing waves and truck connections due to capacity constraints. Four operational levers are introduced to reduce spillage: optimal capacity determination across assets, synchronized wave cut-off design aligned with truck schedules, truck departure-aware order assignment (replacing naive FIFO), and cohort prioritization during demand surges like Big Billion Days. The post is part one of a series, with the next installment focusing on the mathematical optimization behind wave cut-off design.

recent_posts.title: From Noise to Insight: How LLMs Are Transforming Threat Intelligence Analysis
recent_posts.summary: Flipkart's security team built DeepInsight, an LLM-powered platform to automate threat intelligence analysis across 200+ daily alerts. The system ingests unstructured data from multiple sources, normalizes it, and uses Gemini (chosen over GPT-4o and an internal model for its large context window and pricing) to generate structured summaries with true/false positive indicators and recommended actions. Prompt refinement was critical, improving critical data extraction from 60% to 85%. The platform reduced manual triage time by ~75%, enabling analysts to focus on investigation rather than formatting. Future plans include benchmarking Claude and newer Gemini models, and expanding to additional alert types.

recent_posts.title: Solving distributed lock contention with semaphores and fail fast design
recent_posts.summary: Engineers at Flipkart diagnosed a critical system failure during load testing for their Big Billion Days sale. Their Mirana service crashed under load due to excessive contention on a Redis distributed lock. Initial solutions using queuing failed because they violated the 'fail fast' principle. The team ultimately solved the problem by implementing an AtomicInteger-based semaphore to limit concurrent threads attempting lock acquisition. The key insight was optimizing for actual service performance (200-300ms per request) rather than downstream resource limits, reducing allowed concurrency from 128 to 5 threads per pod and achieving stable throughput of 90 QPS across 9 pods.

recent_posts.title: The Science of Unified Ranking: Integrating Ads and Organic Recommendations
recent_posts.summary: Flipkart's engineering team developed a unified ranking system that allows sponsored ads and organic product recommendations to compete dynamically for placement slots, replacing the traditional fixed-slot approach. The solution addresses challenges like data distribution mismatches, fallback risks, and feature parity gaps through a single robust model using isAds flags and cross-features, combined with calibrated scoring functions. The system uses FTRL (Follow The Regularized Leader) algorithm for online learning and multi-stage filtering with CTR and CVR models. Production deployment resulted in a 1.36% increase in organic orders and 3.4% lift in ad revenue, demonstrating that dynamic ranking outperforms static ad placement while maintaining user experience.

recent_posts.title: Unifying the Gates: Building Flipkart’s Centralized API Gateway for 10x Scale
recent_posts.summary: Flipkart built Nexus, a centralized API gateway using open-source APISIX, to replace their fragmented infrastructure where each team managed separate gateway functions. The solution consolidates authentication, rate-limiting, and session management into a unified platform achieving 99.99% availability with sub-10ms p99 latency overhead. The three-plane architecture (management, control, and data planes) uses etcd for real-time configuration updates and deploys across multiple data centers for high availability. The MART organization serves as a case study, showing how Nexus eliminated redundant systems and standardized API management across diverse channels.

recent_posts.title: Flipkart's rapid cloud migration to GCP: strategies and challenges
recent_posts.summary: Flipkart undertook an ambitious cloud migration, moving its Big Data platform to Google Cloud within six months while ensuring zero downtime and high data validation accuracy. Unlike typical phased migrations, Flipkart maintained over 10,000 active pipelines and critical analytics systems throughout the process. The company utilized a combination of specialized engineering teams, strategic tech choices, and customized frameworks to overcome challenges unique to its scale and operations, achieving significant success in its rapid transformation.

recent_posts.title: Showing Delivery SLA at 10x Scale with 1/10th Latency
recent_posts.summary: Flipkart's Promise team aimed to display delivery dates for products on its Search and Browse page within a stringent latency constraint of 100ms for a batch of 100 items. They tackled this challenge by innovating the existing computation flow, optimizing source and vendor capacity stores, and employing caching techniques using Aerospike. These changes enabled real-time delivery date calculations with over 90% accuracy at large scale QPS without compromising user experience.

recent_posts.title: Plato AI: Revolutionising Flipkart’s Data Interaction with Natural Language
recent_posts.summary: Plato AI is transforming data interaction at Flipkart by utilizing natural language queries, enabling non-technical users to access data easily without complex SQL skills. The approach combines AI advancements with a user-friendly natural language query system, focusing on efficiency, accuracy, and democratizing data access. By employing a Domain Specific Language (DSL) and modular architecture, Plato AI provides a scalable and adaptable solution for enterprise data needs.

recent_posts.title: Transforming Data Analytics at Flipkart: Self Serve Insights on Petabytes scale data
recent_posts.summary: Flipkart has transformed its data analytics approach to handle petabyte-scale data by creating an internal platform named Plato. This architecture overcomes challenges related to cost, agility, and accuracy while harnessing GenAI for advanced analytics like automated data analysis and root cause detection. Plato enables self-service BI by simplifying complex data interactions, optimizing query performance, and ensuring data accuracy through a semantic modeling layer.

recent_posts.title: Architecture of Apache HBase Balancer
recent_posts.summary: Apache HBase is an open-source non-relational distributed database modeled after Google's Bigtable. It runs on top of HDFS and features load balancers to ensure optimal resource utilization across nodes. The load balancers, such as StochasticLoadbalancer, can distribute the load based on various factors like the number of API requests, data locality, and region count per server. The HMaster component manages cluster health by assigning regions to regionservers and balancing the load. StochasticLoadbalancer simulates cluster states, applying cost functions and candidate generators to maintain an even load distribution, optimizing cluster performance.

top_posts.title: Addressing Fragmented UI(s) with Micro Frontends
top_posts.summary: Flipkart’s developer console, Podium, transitioned from a monolithic frontend to a micro frontend architecture to overcome challenges such as complex codebases, deployment bottlenecks, and team coordination issues. This new approach allows different teams to build, deploy, and manage their UI components independently, improving scalability, maintainability, and team autonomy. Podium also employs server-side composition and runtime integration with JavaScript for seamless micro frontend integration. Future plans include addressing design inconsistencies and operational complexities.

top_posts.title: Real-Time Data Propagation with HBase: Exploring Change Data Capture and Its Challenges
top_posts.summary: Change Data Capture (CDC) in HBase enables tracking and capturing data changes in real time and making them available for other systems. HBase, a distributed non-relational data store, uses its Write Ahead Log (WAL) to implement CDC. This process supports various business use cases like ad campaigns and e-commerce transactions at Flipkart. The post discusses the architecture, methods of data propagation—Mutation and Cell Based Change Propagation—filters applied, and the challenges encountered in using these methods, providing insights into efficient data tracking and propagation.
